newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan steel group not pessimistic about economy.
newsitem.headline: Japan steel group not pessimistic about economy.

text.p: The Japan Iron and Steel Federation said on Friday that it was not pessimistic about Japan's overall economy and stock market.

"Japan's overall economy is not in a condition that we need to worry about because private capital investment is robust and industries are showing growth," the federation's chairman Takashi Imai told a news conference.
"Share prices are falling but the actual economy is not bad, so we do not need to worry about the stock market," he said.
The federation is one of Japan's major industry groups.

Asked if the government should take steps to deal with share prices, Imai said: "Issues which should advance are advancing and shares which should decline are falling. We should not ask the government for everything."
Imai said the federation forecast Japan's crude steel output in the year to March 31 at 99.5 million tonnes, down 500,000 tonnes from last fiscal year.

But he said business conditions in the steel industry were not bad because demand from the construction industry was seeing year-on-year growth and car exports had been rising sharply since last summer due to the weak yen.
The federation said on Thursday that Japan's crude steel production in calendar 1996 fell 2.8 percent from the previous year to 98.80 million tonnes.
In 1995, Japan's crude steel output was 101.64 million tonnes.
